utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to you one and all. The Status Conference will commence. Madam Registrar, do we have to state the case again, call out the case number again? Yes. Go ahead then, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-96-23/2-PT, the Prosecutor versus Radovan Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In light of the position taken by Mr. Stankovic during the second initial appearance, I would like to limit this Status Conference to inquire of Mr. Stankovic as to his state of health. So could you tell me, please, what your general state of health is like. How do you feel? Do you have anything to impart, anything that you would like to have given you, anything you would like to obtain? Is your state of health good? Yes, I can hear you. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As a detainee, I can say that I feel relatively well, but I would have a remark to make pursuant to your own Rule, Rule 83, about wearing a flak jacket. This irritates me, the wearing of this flak jacket, and according to your Rule, Rule 83, flak jackets are not a means of limiting and restricting freedom, instruments of restraint. They are not a means which prevent an accused from self-injury, injury to others, or to prevent serious damage to property, but this is a secondary matter for me personally, but I should like to request that in my particular case, this instrument of restraint or, rather, the flak jacket not be placed on me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you. Might I just state at this point that pursuant to the Rules, the wearing of a flak jacket is obligatory, in your own interests first and foremost. But what I could do is to ask whether the possibility exists, to inquire whether a flak jacket could be sought which would be lighter and which would not constrain your movements. Do you have any back pain as a result of wearing it or do you suffer from anything of that nature, any illness of any kind?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Well, I don't know. Maybe I do, but I don't know about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Very well. That's all to the good.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You think that you are protecting the accused by placing a flak jacket on him. Under the present circumstances, killings can only be conducted by professionals, and professionals never shoot at the body of a victim, but they target the head or neck. Therefore, I consider that the wearing of a flak jacket is only a provocation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I don't think there's any sense in wearing a flak jacket.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand that you're a professional, but what I would like to assert is that pursuant to the rules applied here, it is compulsory to wear these instruments of restraint. All that I can do is to see whether there is any possibility of you being furnished with a lighter flak jacket which would not weigh heavily on you or cause any unpleasantness when wearing it. I should also like to say, Mr. Stankovic, that in the eyes of the law, you are innocent, and that is a point which I would like and which I shall be insisting upon conveying to you. I would like to convey that idea to you. And nobody can violate that presumption of innocence. Having said that, I would like to inform you that the indictment has conducted -- the Prosecution has conducted -- yes, Mr. Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The problem here is that everything is turned upside down here. Instead of proving my alleged guilt here, what you're doing here is -- or, rather, the Prosecution has brought me in a position here in which I have to prove my innocence, so that the witness of the Prosecution is attributed more value than all my evidence, proof and witnesses. I will bring in 300 witnesses to contest and challenge all those alleged accusations that have been made against me and the charges brought against me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stankovic, be quite certain and assured that before this Tribunal, you are considered innocent until you are proved otherwise. Everything that was contained in the indictment are allegations, and they will have to be proved. Without proof, quite evident proof, clear proof, you are innocent. But this is not the time to enter into the details, and I do ask you to remember that. So it is within this Status Conference -- wait just a minute. I have to interrupt you. You have not even entered a plea yet concerning the charges and counts against you, so the entire procedure is pending, in a way, if I can put it that way, until you enter a plea. So everything is set forward to a period of 30 days. You have 30 days to reflect upon the matter, to think about it, to read and reread the indictment itself, and then we shall hold another initial appearance at which time you will be given the possibility --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say just two things, two sentences. One sentence is linked to the flak jacket. Tell me where it says in your rules that the wearing of a flak jacket is obligatory. That's one point. And secondly, in Rule 96, you state the following: "In cases of sexual assault, no corroboration of the victim's testimony shall be required." That means that if any woman were to state, "You raped me," then nobody, not even God, can refute that. That's what it says here. That's how I understand the reading of this Rule. And there is no justice there. There cannot be any, if that's true. So you have placed me in a position in which I am to prove my innocence, but I am unable to do so because you have your Rules and you adhere to those Rules, and they have nothing to do with justice. I don't mean you personally, I mean this institution of the NATO pact and the New World Order, because this is an institution of the NATO pact and the New World Order. This is a political Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. You're pleading in a marvelous way, but I have to put you right, to correct you. This is not an institution of NATO. I have to say that. It is an institution set up by a Security Council Resolution which represents -- no. Just a minute. I'm talking. You have had enough time to explain your positions. No. I will not allow you to speak further. [In English] No. No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're not going to dwell on that subject. It seems to me that you have not been properly informed about how matters stand. So what I would like to tell you at this point -- no. Please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment. No. Your microphone has been cut off. Please cut off Mr. Stankovic's microphone. Please, sir. First of all, you have declined to enter a plea with respect to the charges and counts against you and read out to you, so the procedure is as follows: We have suspended procedure until you have had time to reflect, and that within the space of 30 days. I would also like to inform you that the Prosecutor has made a request for the application of Article 94(B), I believe, in a motion that was filed in February, and you will have to respond in the space of 14 days following the Rule, as set out in Article 126 bis, unless I'm mistaken. But as you have not entered a plea today as to guilty or not guilty, the time will only start running once you have, in fact, presented your opinion and entered a plea of guilty or not guilty with respect to the charges and counts in the indictment. I should now like to hear the parties. Do they have any matters to raise before we close this Status Conference? And I turn to the Prosecution first. Any matters outstanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you very much. The Defence, would you like to raise any issues?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, after the first Status Conference, Mr. Stankovic and I reached some -- differed in agreement with respect to the organisation of his Defence case and with respect to setting up a Defence team. The secretariat and you personally have been informed thereof. We have informed the Registry. And I as Defence counsel am the sole person having the right to choose my Defence team and determine the concept of our defence case. In 2002, I informed the Registry of the Tribunal, on the 20th of December, that I withdraw my power of attorney to Mr. Stankovic, and Mr. Stankovic did the same, informing me personally and the Registry on the 6th of February, 2002. However, as Defence counsel, adhering to my professional obligations and ethics and the rules determined by the Tribunal, even after that, or rather, ever since December, I still carried out all my duties as Defence counsel so that Mr. Stankovic would not be at a disadvantage in any way in his defence, because it was my duty to do so in keeping with the provisions and rules governing Defence counsel, and I am thinking here of Article 20(A) in particular, the appointment of Defence counsel. I have studied all the documents that I received from the Prosecution, and I sent in a motion with my comments and objections to the first indictment, and the decision made by the Tribunal that a second amended indictment be submitted, which is a decision, in fact, on the first indictment that I objected to on the form of the indictment and the motion tabled by the Defence thereof. Yesterday, I received a response when I reached The Hague. It seems that there was an attempt on the 28th of February, in the afternoon, to send me this by fax, but all I received was the first four pages, and that is a problem that I should like to highlight in particular. As you know, I live in Foca, Srbinje, all the time. That is my permanent residence. The registry has my fax number but it also has my e-mail address, so I would have expected them to send the documents to both those addresses, both by fax, to fax them to me, but also to send them by electronic mail, especially decisions to which I, as Defence counsel, have the right to respond and seek legal remedy. In the future, I should like to request that you bear all this in mind. I should also like to mention that, as Defence counsel, I still went about my work of collecting and amassing possible evidence and proof despite the fact that I was dismissed, although I was not officially relieved of my duties as Defence counsel. And yesterday I informed Mr. Stankovic in part of the results and progress I had made in my investigations. The Registry sent me a letter, Ms. Monica Martinez was the signatory, and informed me that talks had been held with Mr. Stankovic, that they had had an interview with Mr. Stankovic, and that he said he was ready for us to meet again and to assume a final position vis-a-vis future cooperation between ourselves. As I have already stated, yesterday in the Detention Unit, I talked to Mr. Stankovic myself, and I think there is goodwill on his part to accept my Defence case concept. So after the Status Conference that we're holding here today, I shall be having another meeting with Mr. Stankovic to reach a definite decision and agreement as to whether I will continue to be his Defence counsel in this case. I am conscious of the fact that time is passing, but you must have some understanding for me too, because sometimes we have some unexpected problems and conflicting situations that arise, relations that arise between Defence counsel and the accused. I should like to inform you that the Defence has so far always done its best, and if I do reach an agreement with Mr. Stankovic to continue our cooperation in this case - and I think that we shall be able to reach an agreement on that score - then the Defence will do everything in its power, one the team has been completed in the short space of time, we will invest even greater efforts in order to ensure the timely preparation of Mr. Stankovic's defence, to prepare the defence case as best as possible in the shortest space of time. At all events, the Defence has been given a 30-day deadline, and it will send in a motion concerning the second amended indictment as well, with our observations. I should like now to refer to some of the facts that have been put forward by the Prosecution according to Rule 94(B), and this should make it unchallenged between the parties, that is to say the Defence, in the shortest possible space of time, inform the accused of the facts, and once we receive a translation of those facts, we will be in a position to discuss matters with the Prosecution and to file a motion in writing setting out our views, because quite obviously the Defence feels that those facts are now unacceptable as they stand to the Defence team, regardless of the fact that the Prosecution refers to certain positions and judicial notice of adjudicated facts taken in other trials. It is the right of each and every accused to challenge adjudicated facts of this type, especially if we assume the position that the procedure which led up to judicial notice of adjudicated facts, and especially in the proceedings against the Foca group of accused persons, not sufficient attention was paid to establishing those facts. Otherwise, as to the facts proposed and the stipulations made and proposed by the Prosecution, I have already informed my distinguished colleague Mr. Ryneveld that in December, when we had our first meeting, I was ready to discuss those facts. But as there was a certain divergence of views already at that time with respect to the concepts for our Defence case - that is to say between myself and Mr. Stankovic - we didn't see eye-to-eye on all points, without his opinion and agreement, I did not wish to enter discussions of that kind. I did not wish to discuss the facts, given those positions, because that would go against the Rules of Procedure and his rights in particular. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I am sure your goodwill is there, but I hope that you will be able to clarify matters, to clarify the situation that exists between you yourself and Mr. Stankovic as soon as possible. Would you please let us know, because it is an important matter. It is important that Mr. Stankovic has alongside him a Defence counsel and team which would be able to work together with him and ensure a better presentation of his point of view with respect to the charges and counts brought against him. I have been informed that you will be having a meeting with a representative from the Registry in a short while, and I would like to ask you to inform them of the results of your meetings both with Mr. Stankovic and with the OTP to clarify the delicate question of Defence counsel for the accused. I would also like to say that I hope you continue to have close contacts with Mr. Harhoff, our legal officer in chief, who is at your disposal and who will be happy to speed up the procedure. Once again, I should like to thank you all. I think that you have raised the matter with respect to Rule 94(B) and the Prosecutor's motion concerning the application of Rule 94(B). You will have enough time, because the time starts running only after we have held the next initial appearance, which is to say within 30 days. So you'll have time to discuss matters with Mr. Stankovic, to be able to see things clearer, and to pronounce yourselves in the matter. Unless any of the parties would like to raise any other matters at this point, and I think that we've seen to everything, I close the meeting.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mahdi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have not given me an answer: According to what Rule am I obliged to wear a flak jacket?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The registrar can be of assistance to us here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's a very good question, and in answer to it, I can say that it is a rule, it appears, implemented by the Dutch police, and the Dutch police regulations require this measure. I have just been informed of that by the registrar. The only thing I can tell you here and now that is that I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But you say this is an international court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to state that there is an order that must be respected in this court, in this room. It is I alone who am able to give you the floor, the right to speak. So people cannot speak when they feel like it. The Judge has to give the floor to them. I would like that to be clear once and for all. Having said that --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Accepted. It is a rule applied by the Dutch police, as I was saying. There is an agreement reached between the international organisation and the host country, and that is this particular country that we're in. And the country has its rules and its responsibilities. All that I can do and all that is within my power to do is to seek a means, if possible, of having you wear a lighter flak jacket. As far as I know, all the heads of state wear this type of clothing, so I am sure that it's a very sophisticated material that is used. But as I said, I shall do my best to meet your request and lighten your load with respect to wearing a flak jacket.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wore that kind of equipment for ten years. I do have experience with flak jackets, and I can assume what you're going to do now. You'll probably bring in a new rule to stipulate the compulsory wearing of a flak jacket, because you don't -- the rule does not explicitly state this, the compulsory wearing of a flak jacket. I'm sure that you're going to enact a new rule --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stankovic, we don't need to institute a new rule if we already have a rule that is applicable. So you're wrong there. And please believe me when I say that it is in the interests of the person concerned. But let us not enter into a debate which could last for hours. And you say that you are accustomed to wearing a flak jacket. Don't interrupt me, please. You said that you were accustomed to wearing flak jackets over a period of years. That's all the better for you. The only thing that I would like to draw your attention to once and for all, and the matter is closed now, is that it is to protect the person in question that requirements stipulate that flak jackets should be worn. And the Dutch authorities feel obliged and responsible for the security of the entire institution, which means including the Judges themselves. So everybody comes under the security system of the Netherlands. You too.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one moment, please. So you're now mixing up the competencies of the United Nations and the competencies of the state of Holland. And as far as the flak jacket is concerned, if you give me a flak jacket of 100 kilos, I will be able to bear it, but the problem is that every time I wear it, I have to buy a new suit because those flak jackets are dirty, and all kinds -- they're thrown about every which way, you can't get into a car or get out of a car. We need stretchers. I would need to be taken into a car on a stretcher and brought out the same way. So that's why I'm bringing this matter up. It's not practical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I have understood you fully. If there are no other outstanding matters, I adjourn the meeting. Thank you.
